data.title: Yes Bank under pressure: Axis Trustee may seek contempt action against bank over AT1 bonds
data.description:
Yes Bank, in an exchange filing, said Axis Trustee Services Limited, acting as the trustee for the private sector lender's Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds worth ₹8,415 crore, has asked the bank to reinstate the bonds and undertake all necessary corporate actions within three days.

The trustee has warned that failure to comply could prompt it to initiate contempt proceedings against Yes Bank, its directors and officers before the Supreme Court, alleging wilful disobedience of the court's judgment.

In its October 30 filing, Yes Bank said it had communicated with Axis Trustee Services regarding the Supreme Court's judgment concerning the AT1 bond write-off. The trustee responded on October 28, asking the bank to reinstate the bonds and complete all necessary corporate actions within three days.

Yes Bank said it responded to the trustee on October 30, reiterating its commitment to comply with the Supreme Court's judgment and applicable law. The bank also rejected the allegation of wilful disobedience, describing the assertions in the trustee's letter as baseless and without merit. It added that it was examining the judgement and its implications in detail.

The dispute relates to AT1 bonds worth ₹8,415 crore that Yes Bank wrote off in March 2020 as part of its reconstruction process. The Supreme Court upheld the Bombay High Court's ruling that annulled the write-off, paving the way for the bondholders to seek reinstatement.

The trustee has sought the reversal of the write-off entries with the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL), along with the reinstatement of the bonds on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Earlier, CNBC-TV18, citing sources, reported that Axis Trustee had issued a notice dated October 28, giving Yes Bank three days to restore the bonds in accordance with the Supreme Court's ruling.

data.title: CDSL Q2 results: Profit grows 24% to ₹174 crore; demat account base expands 17% YoY
data.description:
Market Infrastructure Institution Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL) reported a 24% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹173.9 crore for the second quarter, compared to ₹140.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue rose 23.7% to ₹395 crore from ₹319 crore in the year-ago period. Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) stood at ₹229 crore, while EBITDA margin improved to 58% from 56% a year ago.

Commenting on the results, Nehal Vora, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer, said, “Despite global macroeconomic volatility, participation in India’s securities market continues to demonstrate resilience. CDSL’s demat account base grew by around 17% year-on-year as of the end of Q2."

He added that this continued growth in market participation drives them to further strengthen their operations and value proposition.

Demat accounts and assets under custody

During the quarter, around 75 lakh new demat accounts were opened with CDSL, as per the company. Its assets under custody (AUC) crossed ₹89 lakh crore.

The company's demat account base grew around 17% year-on-year as of the end of Q2, Managing Director and CEO Nehal Vora said.

Strategic investments and partnerships

During the quarter, CDSL made further investments in India International Bullion Holding IFSC Limited (IIBHL), with the objective of supporting IT infrastructure development, among other areas.

The company also made a strategic investment in the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), an initiative of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

CDSL said that its subsidiary Centrico Insurance Repository Limited entered into a software development partnership agreement with Shoveltech Solutions Private Limited, which operates in the health-tech domain.

Investor education initiatives

CDSL's Investor Protection Fund (IPF) launched a multilingual investor education film with Amar Chitra Katha, based on its 'The Garden of Prosperity' comic, which is available in 12 languages.

In collaboration with Yuva Unstoppable, CDSL IPF began distributing its investor education comics to nearly 21,000 students across 60 schools. It also launched 'Invest Vidya', an investor education YouTube series.

The investor protection fund conducted over 700 investor awareness programmes across India during the quarter.

Shares of Central Depository Services (India) Ltd (CDSL) ended 1.48% lower at ₹1,263 on the NSE on October 30.

data.title: Sarda Energy Q2: Net profit falls 5%, revenue declines 5%; EBITDA margin improves
data.description:
Raipur-based Sarda Group's flagship firm Sarda Energy & Minerals reported a 5.4% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to ₹306 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared to ₹323 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue declined 4.9% to ₹1,453 crore from ₹1,528 crore a year ago. Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) remained largely unchanged at ₹513 crore against ₹512 crore in Q2 FY26.

Segment performance

The company's consolidated segment revenue stood at ₹1,595.74 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to ₹1,739.30 crore in Q2 FY26.

Steel segment revenue declined to ₹397.90 crore from ₹447.38 crore, while Ferro Alloys revenue stood at ₹393.57 crore against ₹396.02 crore.

Power segment revenue fell to ₹800.61 crore from ₹892.36 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Unallocated revenue stood at ₹3.66 crore against ₹3.54 crore.

For the first half of FY27, total segment revenue stood at ₹3,357.73 crore, compared to ₹3,558.90 crore in H1 FY26.

Shares of Sarda Energy & Minerals ended 4.21% lower at ₹438.70 on the NSE on October 30, ahead of earning announcement.

data.title: MeitY launches DEPA handbook to enable secure data sharing for AI training
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- India's artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions could receive a boost through wider access to high-quality datasets, with the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launching a new framework to enable secure data collaboration while protecting privacy, intellectual property and institutional control.

The ministry on Saturday launched the Handbook on Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training at a high-level roundtable in Bengaluru. The handbook was unveiled by S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, with support from the iSPIRT Foundation.

The framework seeks to address challenges that often restrict data sharing, including concerns around privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property and institutional control. It establishes a techno-legal framework for purpose-bound data collaboration, allowing institutions to share data for AI training while retaining control over their information.

The framework combines contractual permissions, controlled computing environments and privacy-enhancing safeguards. It also incorporates data provenance, allowing the origin, permissions and use of data to be tracked throughout the AI training process to ensure accountability and transparency.

"India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to use data responsibly and securely. The DEPA Training Framework enables trusted data collaboration at scale, unlocking access to large-scale datasets for AI training while safeguarding privacy, commercial confidentiality and institutional control," Krishnan said.

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Ajay Kumar Sood highlighted that the framework allows AI models to access data without requiring institutions to transfer the underlying information.

"Under DEPA, the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model," Sood said, adding that the approach could facilitate trusted, multi-party and cross-border data collaboration and accelerate scientific discovery.

He described the framework as India's contribution to global science diplomacy and efforts to develop an inclusive and responsible global AI ecosystem.

Sharad Sharma, Co-founder of iSPIRT Foundation, described the launch as a significant milestone for India's data economy, comparing its importance with the announcement of the Unified Payment Interface (UPI) in February 2016.

Kris Gopalakrishnan, Co-founder of Infosys and Chairman of Axilor Ventures, said the framework could help researchers access diverse datasets to develop more robust AI models while protecting the rights of data custodians and contributors.

The roundtable brought together representatives from government, industry, technology, academia, research and media to discuss trusted data collaboration and its role in advancing AI innovation and public good.

data.title: India to meet liquor firms as domestic giants join foreign peers in Scotch dispute
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indian investigators say bulk Scotch doesn’t qualify for the 75% tariff
  • Diageo, Pernod, Allied Blenders, Radico Khaitan among those told, sources say
  • Indian lobby group warns of hit to local manufacturing
  • About 80% of Scotch imports from Britain arrive in bulk

By Aditya Kalra

India's government will hold talks with liquor companies on Monday after domestic firms joined Diageo and Pernod in expressing alarm about a federal investigation into bulk Scotch imports, according to four sources and an industry letter.

In the first major dispute linked to a historic India-UK trade pact implemented in July, New Delhi has told major companies that bulk Scotch imports are not eligible for the tariff reduction to 75% from 150% agreed in the deal.

The International Spirits & Wines Association of India, a group representing Pernod and Diageo , has privately warned New Delhi that the move to exclude bulk Scotch ​imports could undermine the pact.

The Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies (CIABC) has now joined the protest by flagging a hit to domestic manufacturing, according to an October 27 confidential letter to the government that Reuters is reporting for the first time.

Around 80% of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk to be used to make popular brands, and India's $65 billion alcohol industry had hoped the cut in tariffs would bolster business.

Top Indian commerce ministry officials will on Monday hold closed-door talks with several senior executives of foreign and domestic liquor companies to discuss the issue, said the four people who have direct knowledge of the meeting.

The ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours on Saturday.

Britain has said it is working with India on the issue, and Scottish government has raised the treatment ‌of bulk Scotch with New Delhi, Reuters has reported. India has not commented on the matter.

Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during years of protracted ​negotiations on a UK-India free trade deal, though India, a whisky-loving nation, ultimately agreed ⁠to halve taxes on certain Scotch imports.

INDIAN PEERS SEEK URGENT INTERVENTION

The CIABC's letter said that if bulk Scotch used in Indian manufacturing was not eligible for the lower tariff, "this could create an unintended incentive in favour of importing finished products."

"Such an outcome would run counter to the objective of strengthening domestic manufacturing under Make in India," it added, seeking urgent intervention to avoid disruptions.

The group’s members include listed Indian majors Radico Khaitan , maker of the 8PM brand, and Allied Blenders and Distillers , maker of Officer’s Choice. CIABC and the companies did not respond to queries. All firms have said they comply with the law.

Allied Blenders said in an investor presentation this week it is “one of the largest bulk Scotch importers” and the UK pact would improve its “luxury portfolio accessibility”.

Import tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in ‌India who ⁠have faced demands for large amounts of back tax. Indian officials say they are only enforcing the law of the land.

data.title: Tether's Safety Cushion Nearly Doubles To $8B In A Single Quarter After $1.5B Profit In Third Quarter
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tether's excess reserves nearly doubled to about $7.95 billion at the end of September, from $4.1 billion three months earlier, according to its BDO attestation.
  • The stablecoin issuer earned $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the quarter, and $4.5 billion so far this year, mostly from US Treasury bills and repos.
  • Its $132.4 billion in Treasury exposure is roughly on par with South Korea's holdings, while reserves also included $19.1 billion in gold and $8.4 billion in Bitcoin.

Tether's (USDT) excess reserves nearly doubled in the third quarter, as the issuer of the world's largest stablecoin earned $1.5 billion in profit, mostly from interest on U.S. government debt.

The company's reserves exceeded its liabilities by about $7.95 billion at the end of the September quarter, up from $4.1 billion at the end of June, according to its quarterly attestation, which accounting firm BDO prepared and Tether published on Friday. That buffer was the amount Tether held above what it needed to back every USDT token in circulation.

Tether made $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the third quarter, in line with the previous quarter. It has now earned $4.5 billion so far this year. Most of that came from US Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements, which were short-term loans backed by government securities. The profits came even though USDT's supply changed little. Issuance held at about $184 billion through the first three quarters of the year, despite shifts in the crypto market.

USDT’s price continued to trade flat at nearly $1 over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around USDT remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ over the past day.

What Backs USDT?

Tether held $191.5 billion in total reserves at quarter-end, against $183.5 billion in liabilities. Direct and indirect exposure to U.S. Treasury bills made up $132.4 billion. That exposure was roughly in alignment with South Korea's $134.2 billion in U.S. Treasury holdings and above the United Arab Emirates' (UAE) $116.1 billion, according to data from the U.S. Treasury Department.

The reserves also included over $19 billion in precious metals and roughly $8.4 billion in Bitcoin (BTC), valued at Bitcoin's September 30 closing price of $83,621. The rest included $14.2 billion in secured loans, $4.2 billion in public equities and $6 billion in other investments, the attestation showed.

On Reserves

"Our responsibility is to make sure USDT remains dependable when people need it most, including when markets and financial systems come under pressure," CEO Paolo Ardoino said. According to him, earning $1.5 billion in profit while holding "nearly $8.0 billion in excess reserves,” gave them a “strong foundation for that work."

On X, Ardoino said that USDT's user base had reached a record of more than 700 million people across emerging markets. He called the stablecoin "the biggest financial inclusion success story in the history of humanity."

data.title: Bajaj Electricals gets ₹112.32 crore tax demand for AY 2019-20
data.description:
Bajaj Electricals Limited received an income tax demand of ₹112.32 crore, including interest, for Assessment Year (AY) 2019-20, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing on Friday, October 31.

Bajaj Electricals Tax Notice

The company said that the income tax department disallowed some expenses that it had claimed for the said assessment year. It said the order would not affect its day-to-day business.

The National Faceless Assessment Centre (NFAC) of the Income Tax Department issued the order on October 29 under Section 147 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

The demand arose from the disallowance of expenses, which means the department refused to let the company deduct those costs from its taxable income. AY 2019-20 covers income earned in the financial year 2018-19.

Section 147 allows the tax department to reassess a taxpayer's income when it believes some income has escaped assessment. Faceless assessments are handled online, without any direct meeting between the taxpayer and the officer.

Bajaj Electricals said the Assessing Officer passed the order without giving credit for taxes it had already paid. The order also left out credit for interest under Section 244A of the Act, which deals with interest on tax refunds, the company said.

The filing described both points as omissions by the Assessing Officer.

Company Response

The company said its management was evaluating its legal options, including filing a rectification application or an appeal before the appropriate authority. A rectification application asks the authority that passed an order to correct a mistake in it. An appeal takes the matter to a higher authority.

Bajaj Electricals said any financial impact would be limited to the demand raised and any penalty levied. It said the order had no impact on its operational, financial or other activities.

Bajaj Electricals shares ended 5.81% lower on Friday, October 30, and hit a 52-week low of ₹263.25 during the day. It was the stock's second straight session of losses. The shares have fallen 44.28% so far this year and 49.92% over the past 12 months.

data.title: Dan Ives Says Anthropic IPO Faces A ‘Perfect Storm’ — Aswath Damodaran Warns ‘If One Falls, They Drag The Others Down’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives said that the key question is whether the development ultimately affects investor appetite for Anthropic’s IPO.
  • He added that the amount of money that Anthropic wants to raise could become a concern, particularly as AI companies continue to spend heavily on infrastructure.
  • Damodaran said that the credit rating question could be more significant for lenders than equity investors.

Anthropic’s potential IPO came under fresh scrutiny Friday after a Financial Times report raised questions about whether the AI company could secure an investment-grade credit rating following its public debut.

During a CNBC interview on Friday, Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives and NYU Stern School of Business professor and “Dean of Valuation” Aswath Damodaran discussed what the report could mean for Anthropic’s IPO and the broader AI trade.

This comes amid a report by The Financial Times on Friday that according to Blackstone, Anthropic may not secure an investment-grade rating immediately after going public.

Dan Ives Calls It A ‘Perfect Storm Moment’

Ives described the latest development as a “perfect storm moment” for Anthropic, which he said is central to the ongoing AI buildout.

“It’s the last thing investors want to see because Anthropic foundationally is so key to this AI revolution build out,” Ives said. He added that the key question is whether the development ultimately affects investor appetite for Anthropic’s IPO, while continuing to see the possibility of a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation.

However, Ives said the amount of money Anthropic needs to raise could become a concern, particularly as AI companies continue to spend heavily on infrastructure.

“Just like we’re seeing with Oracle and others, it’s an arms race, and it definitely would put them a bit in the penalty box,” Ives said.

He said investors would ultimately focus on whether Anthropic can demonstrate its business model and potentially regain investment-grade status.

“But then it comes down to as they prove out their model, can they get back to investment grade if such is the case,” Ives said.

Damodaran Warns ‘If One Falls, They Drag the Others Down’

Damodaran said the market environment could be particularly important for Anthropic’s IPO because of the role that sentiment plays in new listings.

“IPOs are all about mood and momentum,” Damodaran said.

“The worst thing that can happen for Anthropic is the mood keeps going the way it is right now. Because that is going to mean that the initial reception, at least, is not going to be as positive as they hoped it would be,” he said.

Damodaran described three groups within the AI ecosystem, which are companies building AI infrastructure, suppliers such as chip companies, and companies including Anthropic and OpenAI.

“They’re all connected at the hip. If one falls, they drag the others down with them,” warned Damodaran, while adding that this interconnection is already playing out in the market.

Why The Credit Rating Matters

Ives and Damodaran also differed somewhat on the significance of Anthropic’s potential credit-rating issue. Damodaran said the rating question could be more significant for lenders than equity investors.

“I think that the rating story is perhaps more significant than it was for the people on the lending side than it is on the equity side,” he said, while questioning the financial commitments being made by young AI companies.

“It’s never made sense,” Damodaran said, referring to companies entering into these contractual commitments like Anthropic for building out AI infrastructure.

Ives, meanwhile, pointed to Anthropic’s position in the enterprise market and its growth potential, comparing the opportunity with OpenAI.

“I think what’s happening today is it’s a tale of two cities,” Ives said, pointing to strong cloud numbers and AI infrastructure spending alongside disruption across areas including memory and advertising.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 1.77%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) fell 3.47%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) closed lower by 1.07%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) fell about 4.45% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) fell nearly 4.33%.

data.title: IGL, Northern Railway join hands to replace LPG, diesel with PNG at 22 locations
data.description:
Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) has signed an agreement with the Delhi Division of Northern Railway to supply piped natural gas (PNG) to 22 railway establishments across Delhi-NCR, as the city gas distributor steps up efforts to replace conventional fuels with natural gas under the government's PNG Drive 3.0.

The agreement will initially facilitate the supply of around 3,000 standard cubic metres of gas per day (SCMD), replacing consumption of approximately 500 kg of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and 2,500 litres of diesel daily, IGL said in a statement.

The proposed conversion will cover railway mechanised laundries, officers' rest houses, base kitchens, running rooms, subordinate rest houses and guard and ticket examiner lobbies across Delhi, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar.

The mechanised laundries at Delhi Sarai Rohilla, Old Delhi, Anand Vihar Terminal, Hazrat Nizamuddin and New Delhi will use PNG for boiler operations.

IGL expects consumption under the initiative to increase to 8,000-10,000 SCMD in the coming years as pipeline infrastructure and connectivity expand across its authorised geographical areas, including Ajmer, Banda, Rewari and Muzaffarnagar.

The agreement, signed on Friday in the presence of senior officials from both organisations, is part of a broader push to expand natural gas consumption among institutional and commercial users and reduce reliance on imported fuels.

"This partnership brings together two major organisations committed to nation building. Indian Railways has chosen IGL as its collaborative partner to replace LPG with PNG and this MoU will facilitate the substitution of a substantial quantity of LPG with natural gas, thereby helping reduce import dependence and the associated subsidy burden," IGL Chairman Subhankar Sen said.

He added that the collaboration could pave the way for a wider transition from LPG to PNG across the Indian Railways network, extending its impact beyond Delhi.

Delhi Division Railway Manager Pushpesh Raman Tripathi said the agreement would help reduce energy costs for the national transporter and that PNG connectivity could subsequently be extended to railway hospitals and residential colonies.

"This MoU will help reduce substantial energy costs for Indian Railways and we plan to extend PNG connectivity to railway hospitals and residential colonies in the future as well," he said.

The partnership comes as IGL intensifies efforts to expand household PNG connections under the government's National PNG Drive 3.0.

On October 28, the company launched promotional incentives offering a Rs 2,000 discount on standard domestic PNG registration charges and Rs 500 worth of free gas after activation of a connection. The initiative seeks to accelerate registrations and gas-in conversions across Delhi-NCR and other authorised areas through outreach programmes and partnerships with resident welfare associations and apartment owners' bodies.

IGL Managing Director Kumar Shanker said the initiative was aimed at extending pipeline-based natural gas to a wider range of institutional consumers, while structured outreach and partnerships with residential associations would help speed up household connectivity.

The twin initiatives reflect the government's broader effort to expand natural gas use in transport, industry, commercial establishments and households. Replacing LPG and diesel with pipeline gas can reduce the need for cylinder handling and fuel storage while providing a continuous supply, although the actual cost and emissions benefits would depend on procurement prices, end-use efficiency and the fuels displaced.

IGL operates city gas distribution networks across 34 districts in 11 geographical areas spanning Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.

Its infrastructure includes more than 30,000 km of pipelines and over 1,000 CNG stations, serving more than 2.5 million CNG vehicles and nearly 3.5 million PNG-connected households.

The railway agreement offers a potential institutional template for expanding PNG adoption across public-sector establishments, while the household incentives seek to build demand at the consumer level. A wider rollout across railway facilities could provide a sizable additional market for city gas distributors and help advance India's efforts to diversify its fuel mix and reduce dependence on imported energy. PTI ANZ ANU

About ReGuest S.P.A:

ReGuest S.P.A is a leading company in Customer Relationship Management (CRM) for hotels with a focus on guest communication. The platform offers a suite of tools and services that help hotels increase direct bookings, enhance the guest experience, and maximize revenue. By integrating artificial intelligence and automation technologies, ReGuest enables hotels to deliver personalized communication to their guests across various channels such as email, SMS, and messaging apps. This individualized approach strengthens guest loyalty and boosts customer satisfaction. ReGuest also provides innovative solutions for managing booking inquiries, creating and sending offers, and analyzing guest data. These features empower hotels to operate more efficiently, improve conversion rates, and make well-informed business decisions. Through continuous development and adaptation to the evolving needs of the industry, ReGuest remains at the forefront of the digital transformation in hospitality. With a strong focus on innovation, customer service, and market leadership, ReGuest positions itself as a trusted partner for hotels worldwide

data.title: Escorts Kubota To Hike Tractor Prices Across Three Brands From November
data.description:
Price revision across Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac ranges will vary by model, variant and geography

Escorts Kubota Limited (EKL) will increase prices across its Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac tractor ranges from November 2026, following the festive season. The company said the revision was driven by rising input costs, including raw materials, energy, logistics and manufacturing expenses.

The price increase will vary across models, variants and geographies within the three tractor portfolios. Revised prices will be available through authorised dealerships.

The company attributed the increase in costs to inflationary trends and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties. It said it had undertaken cost optimisation and operational efficiency initiatives over the past several months to limit the impact on customers. EKL also absorbed a substantial portion of the increased costs.

However, with input costs continuing to remain elevated, the company said the price revision had become necessary to partially offset higher manufacturing and operating expenses.

Escorts Kubota Expands Tractor Portfolio

Alongside the price revision, EKL has continued to expand its tractor offerings across its three brands.

Recent additions include the Farmtrac PROMAXX series, Powertrac Shaurya series and an expanded Digitrac range. The company has also expanded its Kubota portfolio with the NeoStar and MU series.

These product additions, supported by dealer network expansion, are aimed at providing farmers with a wider choice of tractors suited to different agricultural requirements.

Escorts Kubota operates in the agricultural and construction equipment segments. Its product portfolio includes tractors under the Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac brands, along with specialised agricultural machinery and construction equipment.

The company has a dealer network serving customers across India and international markets.

data.title: Reliance Jewels Onboards Gopa Kumar To Lead Business
data.description:
The retail veteran joins Reliance Jewels after a seven-year stint as COO of Bhima Jewels, bringing over two decades of experience

Reliance Jewels, part of Reliance Retail, has appointed Gopa Kumar as Head of Reliance Jewels, bringing an experienced retail executive on board to lead the jewellery business. Kumar announced his new role through a LinkedIn post, stating that he was looking forward to building on the brand's legacy and identifying fresh opportunities for growth.

He joins Reliance Jewels after a seven-year stint as Chief Operating Officer at Bhima Jewels, where he had been associated with the retailer since 2019. During his tenure, he oversaw operations at the jewellery business before announcing his departure and return to Mumbai.

Kumar brings more than two decades of experience across organised retail and consumer-facing businesses. His professional background includes leadership positions at Future Group, Shoppers Stop, Hindustan Unilever, Next Retail and Future Retail, among others.

His experience spans business strategy, profit and loss management, retail operations, category management, marketing, digital initiatives and business expansion. He has also worked across different retail formats, including department stores, convenience retail, e-commerce, luxury, lifestyle and speciality retail.

At Reliance Jewels, Kumar is expected to focus on business strategy, retail expansion, brand development and customer experience, alongside driving revenue growth and operational performance. His responsibilities will also include strengthening merchandising and product strategy, digital and omnichannel initiatives, and organisational capabilities.

The appointment comes as Reliance Jewels continues to operate within India's organised jewellery retail market, with a portfolio spanning gold, diamond and silver jewellery and a nationwide network of company-owned showrooms.

data.title: Advance Gold Helps Optimise Our Working Capital: Sky Gold and Diamonds CFO
data.description:
Siddharth Sipani outlines how the model is reducing inventory funding requirements and supporting higher manufacturing volumes

For Sky Gold and Diamonds, managing working capital has become an important part of its growth strategy as it seeks to balance higher production volumes with cash flow discipline. The company reported positive operating cash flow of approximately Rs 30 crore in Q1 FY27, alongside 78 per cent revenue growth, following a year of negative operating cash flow.

Siddharth Sipani, CFO of Sky Gold and Diamonds, discusses the operational changes behind this shift, the role of the Advance Gold model, export opportunities and the financial priorities of a growing B2B jewellery manufacturer.

You have spoken about deliberately holding back from pushing sales growth even higher to protect that cash flow. What did it take internally to make that trade-off between growth and cash discipline?

Q1 FY27 marked an important step in our financial progression, with strong revenue growth accompanied by positive operating cash flow. Our focus has been on sustaining that balance across sales growth, profitability and working capital.

We have focused on receivables, inventory and business mix, while deploying part of the cash generated by gold jewellery into higher-margin studded products. Approximately Rs 30 crore of positive operating cash flow was achieved in the June 2026 quarter alongside 78 per cent revenue growth, reflecting the progress of this approach.

Sky Gold raised Rs 270 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement. How are you thinking about deploying that capital alongside the company's shift towards its 'Advance Gold' model aimed at reducing inventory risk?

The QIP supported an earlier phase of expansion. Raised in October 2024, the proceeds were almost fully utilised by December that year towards the working capital requirements of the Group. Due to this fundraising, the company has been able to scale its operations from 250 kg to 750 kg. The Advance Gold model of the business helps in optimising the company's working capital needs, and funds released from this business model are deployed towards serving other customers. This helps in better overall capacity utilisation and achieving higher volumes and PAT for the Group.

Sky Gold has been moving towards reducing inventory risk and improving capital efficiency through this Advance Gold approach. What has been the biggest operational change internally to make that shift work while the business keeps growing this fast?

As Advance Gold becomes a larger part of our business, operational visibility is increasingly important to capital efficiency. Our technology and enterprise resource planning (ERP) initiatives support better tracking of data and the movement of goods across the organisation.

Alongside this, our existing facilities offer headroom for growth. Higher utilisation improves cost absorption and allows us to generate more output from infrastructure already in place. At the same time, we have existing manufacturing capacity that can support further growth. As we improve utilisation, we can scale the business more efficiently.

Exports to the Middle East and Southeast Asia have been a growing part of Sky Gold's business alongside deepening retail partnerships in India. How do you see that export mix evolving as the company scales further?

Exports are an important part of our growth strategy, both for market diversification and their attractive financial profile. We are targeting an export contribution of around 20 per cent by FY30, supported by our Dubai base and established presence in the UAE, Bahrain, Singapore and Malaysia.

We are also developing opportunities in the UK and Japan. Our participation in the London jewellery exhibition generated initial order interest of Rs 30-45 crore from buyers across these markets. Strengthening our overseas teams and channels gives us a broader platform to build this business.

Before joining Sky Gold, you spent over eight years as Group CFO at Gold Star Jewellery and earlier led M&A financial due diligence at EY. What from leading due diligence on other companies' deals has shaped how you run finance at a fast-scaling listed company now?

My experience across audit, M&A consulting and the jewellery industry has given me exposure to businesses at different stages and across different functions.

At Sky Gold, that experience helps me look at growth from both a financial and operational perspective. We are focused on improving profitability, cash flow and working capital as the business expands.

Technology is another important part of this journey. With better ERP systems and data visibility, we can make decisions faster and manage a growing business more effectively.

Sky Gold operates as a B2B gold jewellery manufacturer supplying organised retailers rather than selling directly to consumers. What is distinct about managing the finance function for a B2B manufacturing model in an industry that is traditionally thought of as consumer-facing?

The B2B model means our financial focus is very closely linked to manufacturing and working capital. We look at areas such as receivables, inventory, profitability and capacity utilisation on a continuous basis.

Advance Gold is particularly useful in this model because customers provide the gold, allowing us to focus on the manufacturing side without the same working capital requirement.

Exports also add to the efficiency of the model, with higher return on capital employed (ROCE) and lower receivable days. Overall, our focus is on building a sustainable business that can grow at scale while becoming more efficient and generating stronger returns.

data.title: Shraddha Bhatt Dave Takes Over As EMA India Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
The appointment takes effect from 30 October following the company's takeover by new management and the resignation of its previous CFO

EMA India has appointed Shraddha Bhatt Dave as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP), effective 30 October 2026. The appointment follows the recent takeover of the company by new management and the resignation of the previous CFO.

The Board of Directors approved the appointment at a meeting held on Friday, 30 October 2026, based on recommendations from the Audit Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The board noted that the company had been identifying a suitable candidate to fill the vacancy created by the former CFO's departure.

Shraddha Bhatt Dave is a Chartered Accountant with over 15 years of experience in financial governance, accounting, audit assurance and regulatory compliance within multinational environments.

Her professional experience includes managing statutory audits, Goods and Services Tax (GST) and tax compliance, as well as cross-border financial reporting under Indian and US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) standards.

She has also worked on strengthening internal control frameworks, identifying financial irregularities and improving transparency in finance operations.

In the same board meeting, the directors accepted the resignation of Awashesh Dixit as Secretarial Auditor. Dixit, a Practising Company Secretary holding Membership No. F10860 and Certificate of Practice (COP) No. 15398, cited his inability to continue in the role. His cessation was effective 30 October 2026.

Regulatory Disclosure Details

The company disclosed the appointments and resignation under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

data.title: Shyam Metalics Q2 results: Company records 88% YoY jump in net profit; margins improve
data.description:
Shyam Metalics has announced its results for Q2 of FY27 on Saturday, October 31. The Kolkata-based company reported strong numbers, with profit and margin figures improving on a year-on-year basis.

Shyam Metallics Q2 Results

The company reported a major 88.5% YoY jump in its net profit, with the profit figure for the September-bound quarter coming in at ₹493.4 crore, as against ₹261.8 crore in Q2 of FY26. When it comes to the top-line numbers, the metal company recorded revenue of ₹5,960 crore in the quarter gone by, which was higher than the previous year's ₹4,467 crore. This marked a year-on-year rise of 33.4% in revenue numbers.

Now, when we look at the profitability of the company over the previous quarter, the company's Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation, or EBITDA, surged by 52.6%, with EBITDA for the quarter rising to ₹823 crore, compared to ₹539 Cr in 2025. Finally, the company also improved margin to 13.8%, with a 170-basis-point rise from the previous cycle's 12.1%.

Q1 Recap Of Shyam Metallics

Sequentially speaking, in Q1FY27, the company's net profit rose by 18% year-on-year, reaching ₹345 crore compared to ₹282 crore previously. For the quarter, revenue increased by 23% from the previous year, amounting to ₹5,455 crore, up from ₹4,423 crore.

Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) for the quarter was ₹765 crore, reflecting a 32% increase from the ₹580 crore reported in the same quarter last year. Additionally, the EBITDA margin for this period improved by 90 basis points from the previous year, rising to 14% from 13.1%.

Stock Performance

A quick look at the stock performance leads us to a stock that has had a strong showing in the recent past; in the latest session, on Friday, the company's shares rose by over 2%.

In the past month, the share price has increased in value by 10%, and 10 months into 2026, Shyam Metallics' shares have surged by over 37% this year. The current stock price sits at ₹1163 per piece, away from the 52-week high of ₹1,240.50 per piece.
